sample_unit: rare diagnostic cases (200 reasoning traces; 5,600 expert-physician annotations)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under progressive information masking and reasoning-to-output mismatch versus expert annotations
links.effect: GPT-4o-mini accuracy dropped from 95.0% to 32.5% under information scarcity; 68.6% reasoning-to-output mismatch; standalone automated evaluations can substantially overestimate clinical reliability.
links.quote: These results suggest that standalone automated clinical evaluations can substantially overestimate clinical reliability without expert-grounded validation.

links.outcome: Whether LLM-as-a-Judge approvals agree with human-verified clinically incorrect outputs
links.effect: On a human-verified failure set (n=142), GPT-4o-mini approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs; HuatuoGPT-o1 approved all validly scored failures and showed positive self-preference bias.
links.quote: GPT-4o-mini approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs, while HuatuoGPT-o1 approved all validly scored failures and showed a positive self-preference bias.

unlisted_practices: Progressive information masking to stress-test LLM diagnostic reasoning
Evaluating reasoning traces separately from final answers to detect reasoning-to-output mismatch

screen.reason: The study empirically assesses LLM clinical reasoning and evaluates the reliability of deployment validation methods (specifically comparing automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluation against human-expert clinical review).

primary.practice: expert-grounded human-in-the-loop validation vs automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
